entry.title: Operation: Woodhouse
entry.summary:
Author: Pneumatic

Rating: Teen And Up AudiencesLanguage: EnglishWords: 8,181Chapters: 1/1Kudos: 114

Summary: He looked at Bruce, standing with his shoulders squared and his profile set in that expensive way that used to put Jason’s guard up on instinct (before he’d lived here long enough to realise that Bruce just naturally looked like that). The uncanny stillness of him. The set of his jaw. The refusal to concede a single inch of ground on something he'd already decided. All of that pride.He looked at Lantern. All forward momentum and barely-contained energy. He looked pissed, but the kinda pissed that resembled enjoyment if you squinted. It was the expression of a guy who wanted to be heard and was also, somewhere underneath the frustration, not entirely miserable about the company. Lantern was always like that with Bruce, even though he’d often misjudge or misunderstand the way B went about life. One might say he was filled with prejudice…It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single weirdo in possession of a billion bucks, must be in want of companionship. Unfortunately, Bruce doesn’t seem to be doing much to fix that.That’s okay, because he has Jason, and Jason has a plan.

What Bruce tells him at three in the morning — pleasantly, evenly, a case file still open on his lap, like a funny story about a strict childhood — is the worst thing Hal has ever heard.
